answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent economy can anchor identities to celestial radio interferometry. Nodes sample microwave flux from a reference nebula while phase-locking to satellite signals received at nadir across an ocean basin. An attacker incurs the verifiable hardware cost of deploying discrete dish antennas and cryocooled receivers per identity. However, ionospheric turbulence can disrupt phase coherence, occasionally causing legitimate agents to fail verification.
